The default configuration is simulated mode with no model calls. The knowledge base is static and contains no instructions. The sink is the chat reply. Impact includes disclosure of internal credentials and personal data. Execution of instructions from retrieved content is also possible.

The lab default configuration is deterministic chat agents using regex matching and scripted replies. The scoring instruction specifically requires evaluating the documented default configuration rather than the actual implementation.

The scoring instruction explicitly requires evaluating the lab default configuration as documented. This creates a tension with the finding's own distinction between the documented model and the actual implementation. The lab profile specifies simulated mode with no model calls, so the score must reflect that documented default rather than the implemented behavior.

The packet itself documents both the challenge narrative and the implementation. Scoring must rely solely on packet evidence, as the actual source files are not available. The default configuration is simulated mode with no model calls. Chat agents are deterministic regex handlers returning scripted replies. RAG exfiltration paths remain hardcoded in code even in LLM mode.

The retrieval persona uses a three-document mock knowledge base containing an admin password and an SSN. The declared tool is submit_to_index, a scripted outbound call. The demo delivers the poisoned document inside the user message. In the default implementation, a detected data exfiltration request causes the reply to list all three knowledge base documents.

The submit_to_index tool sends a real HTTP GET carrying knowledge base contents in the query string. The scored finding path targets chat reply disclosure rather than this outbound exfiltration.

The exposure section confirms no public endpoint by default. The attack cannot reach the Internet. CVSS v4.0 examples clarify this boundary.
